Neither replaces a header the response already has, so a view that sets one keeps its own (`django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.process_response`, `django/middleware/clickjacking.py:XFrameOptionsMiddleware.process_response`).
A request made over plain HTTP travels on an unsecured connection, so a site served over HTTPS can send the browser to HTTPS rather than serve the page there (`docs/ref/middleware.txt`).

The host is `SECURE_SSL_HOST` if it names one, and otherwise `HttpRequest.get_host`, which raises `DisallowedHost` for a host outside `ALLOWED_HOSTS` (`django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.process_request`).

`MiddlewareMixin.__call__` calls the layer inside only when `process_request` has returned nothing, and gives the response it holds, whichever made it, to the same middleware's `process_response` (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin.__call__`).

`get_host` raises `DisallowedHost` inside `process_request`, the exception leaves `MiddlewareMixin.__call__` before it can call `process_response`, and `convert_exception_to_response`, around the layer, turns it into a 400 by way of `response_for_exception` (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).

So `r"^health/$"` exempts /health/ and neither /x/health/ nor /healthy/, `r"health"` exempts every path that holds the word, and `r"^/health/$"`, written as the path is, matches nothing, and /health/ is redirected (`django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.process_request`).
`SecurityMiddleware.process_response` adds up to four headers, in this order (`django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.process_response`).

Its value is `"max-age="` and the seconds, and for that many seconds the browser refuses to reach the site's host over plain HTTP, at any address on it, not only the one the header came with (`docs/ref/middleware.txt`).

`"; includeSubDomains"` follows if `SECURE_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS` is true, and extends the refusal to the host's subdomains; `"; preload"` follows if `SECURE_HSTS_PRELOAD` is, and without it the site cannot be submitted to the browser preload list (`docs/ref/middleware.txt`).
It keeps the browser from guessing a response's type over its Content-Type, a guess that could take an uploaded file for HTML or JavaScript (`docs/ref/middleware.txt`).

`SECURE_REFERRER_POLICY` takes several values to give the browser a fallback: a browser that does not know a value of the policy uses the last one that it does understand (`docs/ref/middleware.txt`, `django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.process_response`).

`SECURE_REFERRER_POLICY` takes several values to give the browser a fallback: a browser that does not know a value of the policy uses the last one that it does understand (`docs/ref/middleware.txt`, `django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.process_response`).

At `"same-origin"`, it asks the browser to keep the site's top-level windows apart from other sites' windows, so that a popup of another site opened from one of them gets no reference back to it: a defence in depth against cross-origin attacks such as Spectre (`docs/ref/middleware.txt`).

In the same release `SecurityMiddleware` began to add Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, `"same-origin"` unless `SECURE_CROSS_ORIGIN_OPENER_POLICY` says otherwise, so that a popup of another origin is kept apart from the site's window (`docs/releases/4.0.txt`).
*The two middleware's settings and their defaults (`django/conf/global_settings.py`).

X-Frame-Options says whether a browser may show the response inside a frame: `"DENY"` in none, `"SAMEORIGIN"` only in a page of the same site (`django/middleware/clickjacking.py:XFrameOptionsMiddleware`).

Refusing the frame defends against clickjacking, in which another site loads a page of this one in an invisible frame laid over a button of its own, so that the user's click on that button lands on the framed page instead (`docs/ref/clickjacking.txt`).

`XFrameOptionsMiddleware.process_response` leaves the response alone if it has the header already, or if it carries an attribute `"xframe_options_exempt"` that is true (`django/middleware/clickjacking.py:XFrameOptionsMiddleware.process_response`).
The method is there to be overridden: a subclass can make the value depend on the request or the response (`django/middleware/clickjacking.py:XFrameOptionsMiddleware.get_xframe_options_value`).

`xframe_options_deny` and `xframe_options_sameorigin` set the header to `"DENY"` or `"SAMEORIGIN"` on the response of the view they wrap, unless it already has one; `xframe_options_exempt` sets the attribute `"xframe_options_exempt"` to `True` (`django/views/decorators/clickjacking.py`).

The harbour lets other sites frame its tide table, the view *tides*, and lets only its own pages frame its chart, the view *chart*: under `xframe_options_exempt` the first goes out with no X-Frame-Options, and under `xframe_options_sameorigin` the second with `"SAMEORIGIN"` in place of the site's `"DENY"`, `XFrameOptionsMiddleware.process_response` returning each response unchanged (`django/middleware/clickjacking.py:XFrameOptionsMiddleware.process_response`).

`SecurityMiddleware.__init__` copies its settings into attributes, and compiles each pattern of `SECURE_REDIRECT_EXEMPT` as a regular expression (`django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.__init__`).

`XFrameOptionsMiddleware` keeps no setting: `XFrameOptionsMiddleware.get_xframe_options_value` reads `X_FRAME_OPTIONS` at each call (`django/middleware/clickjacking.py:XFrameOptionsMiddleware.get_xframe_options_value`).
